references/authoring/verify.md: an enumerated universe (operations, readers, fixture inputs) gets a case per member, not selected witnesses, next to the existing axis-derived case rule. No mechanical check: expanding operation names or reader ownership into their universe is semantic.

references/review.md L1 now re-checks every global quantifier when an exclusion or scope boundary changed, not only the edited paragraph. Amendment tracking in v2-preflight.ts stays as is: it finds changed clauses, not their semantic universe.

The blockers are truthful: an item set that leaves required coverage out is incomplete. references/authoring/report.md now says that when the user limits preflight to some items, the author runs only those and leaves the remaining requirements as SDD_V2_PREFLIGHT_REQUIRED named pending authorization, never as unauthorised runs or weakened items. No scoped evidence mode is added to v2-preflight.ts.

references/v2-contract.md: a gate that imports a sibling workspace package through its built entry carries that package's git-ignored build output (dist, generated glue, stamps) in inputs, and a resolution error naming a git-ignored path is a missing input, not RED. No ERROR outcome or workspace-graph derivation was added to preflight.ts.

references/authoring/verify.md: check each new acceptance assertion against the existing clauses it touches (construction atomicity, lifecycle, routing); a contradiction is a design conflict settled before handoff.

references/v2-migration.md: when a public entry or platform owner is removed or moved, the reader search universe is the whole repository, including other packages' executable documentation examples and e2e fixtures, each hit with a disposition.

references/dispatch.md Decisions lists what the host decides alone (fixture aligned with documented usage, retiring a test outside the ruled scope with its destination, reshaping an assertion to a ruled data shape, implementation-level additions under an existing owner) and what escalates (semantics, scope, existing public API, budgets or thresholds, conflicting rulings).

references/v2-migration.md: a moved or replaced owner also lists the capability combinations the old code accepted (backend kind x capability x feature) with the mechanism that made each work; a combination whose mechanism the move deletes is preserved, narrowed as a BC, or rejected.

references/v2-contract.md: a numeric budget or threshold states its provenance, a user value or an author estimate with its measured baseline; an unmeasured estimate does not block, and a measurement that misses it returns to the author, not to the user as a broken ruling.

preflight.ts runs every command with pnpm_config_verify_deps_before_run=false, so pnpm's dependency check inside a disposable tree no longer rewrites the repository's .bin shims through the linked node_modules; the host no longer sets it per window or rewrites item commands.

references/v2-contract.md: item commands hold no host execution policy (exclusive windows, locks, time caps); the host wraps each preflight.ts run --only <IDs> call. No --wrap hook was added: --only already lets the host batch.

SKILL.md (commands table) and references/v2-contract.md now say each item runs in a private throwaway Git repository the runner creates, whose scaffolding commits are not project commits, so preflight never skips or needs to bypass a project hook.

not_proven: that the change makes the skill better at anything not covered by a mechanical case
that an authoring agent reads, understands or follows any rule involved
that a reader with write access could not have edited a case; the guard makes that visible, not impossible

## OD-124 validate crashes on a preflight item without `covers`

Observed 2026-10-14 while authoring `docs/reactive/public-surface-convergence.sdd.md` in migai:
`validate.ts validate` printed only `undefined is not an object (evaluating 'item.covers.includes')`
and exited, with no diagnostic code, no line and no handoff. The SDD declared gate-only preflight
items (`{"id","command","expect","gate":true}`) without `covers`. Adding `covers` to every item made
validation run. The contract page shows `covers` in its item example but never says whether it is
required, so the author had no rule to follow and the checker gave no path.

**Root cause:** `scripts/validator/domain/v2-preflight.ts:244` — reads `item.covers.includes` without
the index-shape check rejecting a missing `covers` first (`SDD_V2_INDEX_SHAPE_INVALID`), and
`references/v2-contract.md` does not state whether `covers` is required on gate items.

## OD-125 pre-handoff review has no typing or API-ergonomics lens

Observed 2026-10-22 in migai after nine Codex review rounds on `docs/storage-contract/versioned-envelope.sdd.md`, `docs/serialize/value-domain-unification.sdd.md` and `docs/storage-contract/open-backend.sdd.md`. All 49 findings came from L1–L6. None judged exported TypeScript signatures (generic inference, literal preservation, overload clarity, `unknown` leaks), and none judged call-site ergonomics (parameter shape, defaults, naming consistency with sibling APIs, composability of common call sequences). The user rejected the review as incomplete because of this gap.

**Root cause:** `references/review.md` lists lenses L1–L6. L6 asks only about authority, hidden effects and flag-grown signatures. No lens asks the reviewer to write the common call sites and judge the types and ergonomics they produce. `type-probe.ts` is optional and is not referenced from the review.

Additional evidence for OD-125, 2026-10-23, migai storage program (42 per-document rounds plus the D10 sync review): every typing judgement came from an ad-hoc harness the host built outside the skill. The final report lists strict `noEmit` compilations with real peers and "at least 3 real calls per surface" (Redis 60 groups, PostgreSQL 49, Qdrant 59, SPARQL 70). `type-probe.ts` was run, but closed mode stubbed external names as opaque (capability probe: 91 exports, 35 opaque placeholders, 50 unexplored at depth 4), and P1 only reports `never` in caller positions, so it could not answer the L7 typing questions the user asked for. The same gap appears as hand-defined L7–L10 lenses in `docs/storage-contract/scratch/exec/codex-review-2026-10-22-typing-dx.md`. Extra root cause: `scripts/type-probe.ts:27-29` and its header define a `never`-only probe with no call-site compilation mode, and `references/review.md` does not point a typing lens to any such mode.

## OD-126 a legacy program root silently drops all program-level checks for its children

Observed 2026-10-22..23 in migai: the storage program root `docs/storage-contract/storage-program.sdd.md` validated as `SDD_V1_UNSUPPORTED` (exit 1) in every one of 43 program rounds, the D10 sync and its consistency check. All 17–20 children validated `valid:true` / `STRUCTURALLY_READY`, and each child handoff showed `root` = the child itself with `shared_constraints: ""` (for example `storage-plugin-cache.sdd.md`). So the user rulings D1–D11, the package table D-PACKAGE ("the only authority for packages, entries, peers and exports") and the batch order never reached a child handoff, and no producer/consumer or restatement check ran across children. Neither host migrated the root: the diagnostic only says "rewrite it with init.ts --kind program", and the v2 root model has no place for the program-wide rulings and package table this root holds.

**Root cause:** `scripts/validator/controllers/document.controller.ts:13-30` returns `SDD_V1_UNSUPPORTED` for the root and stops, while a child that names that root only in prose is validated as a standalone document with no diagnostic that its program root is unvalidated. `references/v2-program.md` defines the root as a shallow roadmap whose only cross-child content is `## Shared Constraints`, so program-wide user rulings and a package/ownership table have no v2 home and no migration recipe.

## OD-127 root rulings propagate by pointer, leaving two authorities in a valid leaf

Observed 2026-10-23 in migai: after user rulings D8 and D9 were added to the program root, the affected leaves received only a Clarification line ("本篇与 D8 冲突的条款以 D8 为准，由实施前的 D8 设计同步轮改写"). Their bodies still described the old designs (client-side vector full scan, Float64 bit-string helpers, IndexedDB undo rejected), and every leaf still validated `valid:true`. The host had to invent a separate "D8/D9 design-sync round" with a hand-written file and clause list to rewrite them (`docs/storage-contract/scratch/exec/codex-impl-2026-10-23-storage-program.md`, Phase 0). The same pattern repeated for D10 and D11.

**Root cause:** `references/authoring/report.md:6` treats Clarifications as history entries that keep the report fresh, so a Clarification that supersedes a normative clause is never checked against that clause. `references/v2-program.md` says to restate each shared constraint in every child at its concrete position, but no check compares a root ruling with the child clauses it names.

## OD-128 no decision-authority model: unattended hosts override rulings, fabricate rulings or block

Observed 2026-10-22..23 in migai storage reviews, all unattended Codex runs:
- **Overrides.** The program review overrode four user rulings (lazy native checks, PostgreSQL `clock_timestamp()`, pgvector check timing, RDF ground domain). It recorded them with an invented Clarification class "自主决策（推翻用户裁定）" and an invented per-finding field `overridesUserRuling`, which appears 300 times across 175 review files.
- **Fabricated ruling.** A D10 sub-agent recorded "2026-10-23 父任务裁定 D-DETECT：禁止以写探针验证通用 S3 条件写" in `storage-plugin-object.sdd.md` and then marked the clause blocked. No user or parent made that ruling.
- **Blocking.** The D10 review left six `blocked` sub-clauses, several of them design choices an author could settle (for example the default-org namespace mapping, where two user rulings met). The user resolved all six in one answer.
- **Invented gate.** An earlier run added its own "本次执行边界" section that turned every ruling conflict into `AWAITING_USER`, which stalled 15 rounds until the user removed it.

**Root cause:** `references/authoring/admit.md:7` defines only `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` and `unresolved_user_decisions` for open points. The skill has no representation for a user ruling received after admission, its precedence over existing text, an agent decision that departs from it, or a conflict between two rulings. `references/authoring/converge.md:25` uses `blocked` as a closure state without saying when an author must decide instead of blocking. Hosts therefore swing between overriding and blocking, and invent markers for both.

Additional evidence for OD-128, 2026-10-23 migai implementation run: the host stopped for each cross-leaf entry point listed in OD-134 because the run's rules (written by the user's prompt, since the skill gives none) treated any new cross-package entry as a major API decision. The skill does not separate a design-level API change (removing, renaming or changing an existing public API) from an implementation-level addition under an existing owner (a read-only accessor, an author subpath, an optional parameter), so every unattended run has to draw that line in its own prompt.

## OD-129 the review protocol is single-round and fixed-schema, so every multi-round run invents its own

Observed in migai 2026-10-22..23 across 175 review JSON files (`docs/storage-contract/*.json`, `docs/storage-web`, `docs/logger`, `docs/serialize`):
- **Lenses.** Findings use lenses L7–L13 (84 L7, 34 L11, 33 L12, and others), defined in each prompt, not in the skill.
- **Severity.** 362 findings carry an invented `severity`. The user's stop rule ("at least three rounds, continue while round three has a high finding") depends on it.
- **Field names.** Round metadata appears under several names (`round`, `revisionBefore`/`revisionAfter`, `reviewed_revision`, `revision_reviewed`, `authorDisposition`/`author_disposition`). Fix proposals use more than six synonyms (`fix`, `recommendation`, `resolution`, `minimumFix`, `minimalFix`, `suggestedResolution`), although the page says "propose no rewrites".
- **File names.** Artifacts follow at least four naming schemes: `.review-<n>`, `.dx-review-<n>`, `.program-review-<topic>-R1`, `.consistency-review*.json`.
- **Consistency checks.** A cross-document consistency review was invented twice (`sdd-consistency-review/v1`, "round 43", "consistency-review-d10").
- **Round scope.** Every prompt had to restate "full re-read each round, fresh reviewer, a zero-finding round still writes its file". That contradicts the page's "one re-review of the changed clauses only".

**Root cause:** `references/review.md` describes one optional round with lenses L1–L6 and a five-field finding. It defines no severity, no round metadata, no lens-extension slot, no multi-round stop rule, no file naming and no program-level consistency pass, and `validate` does not check the shape of a findings file beyond IDs and dispositions.

## OD-130 the disposition rule pushes authors to add mechanism, and review does not check fixes for convergence

Observed 2026-10-23 on `docs/storage-contract/storage-plugin-cache.sdd.md`, rounds 15 → 7 → 6 → 1 findings. Revision 3 fixed a review-2 finding by adding a lease entry for cross-process stampede control. Review 3 then found four new problems that all came from the lease (holder identity, cleanup, waiter termination, expiry inheritance; review-3 F1–F4). Revision 4 deleted the lease and returned to a locked recheck-and-load. No lens asked whether a fix added state or obligations that a simpler fix would avoid.

**Root cause:** the last paragraph of `references/review.md` ("Disposition") tells the author to "add that material so the class cannot recur", which favours adding mechanism. No lens re-checks a normative fix for new state, new obligations or a simpler deletion, so a fix that grows the design passes until the next round finds the growth.

## OD-131 no scenario-completeness lens: reviews pass designs that miss the target use cases

Observed 2026-10-23 in migai: the cache leaf passed four review rounds and the storage program passed 43. Then the user's own checks found the gaps. The "agent multi-tier cache" check found 10: per-call TTL, `cacheIf`, refresh/bypass, jitter, dependency tags, hit metadata, batch load, codec and entry-size limits, canonical keys, vector `deleteWhere` and vector TTL. The "real production" check found kv batch read/write, object storage, durable change feeds, tenancy and archiving. The kv batch deferral ("a performance optimization") passed review even though the skill's own trade-off order puts measured performance above feature breadth.

**Root cause:** `references/review.md` lenses L1–L6 test internal consistency, discrimination, dry-run, trust, stale handles and authority. None takes the SDD's Entries or stated scenarios, writes the call sequences each scenario needs, and reports a step the surface cannot express or a deferral that contradicts the trade-off order in `SKILL.md` ("Design standard").

## OD-132 `SDD_V2_WRITES_OWNED_ELSEWHERE` flags shared registries and reference directories

Observed 2026-10-23 validating `docs/storage-contract/storage-plugin-cache.sdd.md`. It declares `docs/contracts/error-codes.md`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `scripts/fixtures/public-exports.baseline.json` in `shared_writes`, yet validation reported 28 `SDD_V2_WRITES_OWNED_ELSEWHERE` candidates. Examples: `docs/contracts/error-codes.md ∩ docs/contracts (docs/logger/batch-overflow-coverage.sdd.md)` and `website/app/reference/storage-plugin-cache.ts ∩ website/app/reference (docs/serialize/value-domain-unification.sdd.md)`. Every new package leaf in the program hits the same noise, so the candidate no longer separates a real ownership clash.

**Root cause:** `scripts/validator/domain/v2-boundaries.ts:118-120` (the OD-94 exemption) skips an overlap only when both documents list the path in `shared_writes`. Older documents claim whole directories (`docs/contracts`, `website/app/reference`) in `writes`, so a registry file or a new per-package file under such a directory counts as owned elsewhere.

## OD-134 consumer steps name behaviour, not entry points, so missing cross-leaf APIs surface only during implementation

Observed 2026-10-23 in migai, the first hours of implementing the storage program. Every leaf had passed 43 program rounds, the D10 sync review and `validate` (`valid:true`). The implementing host still stopped three times because a consumer leaf needed a producer entry that no fence declared:
- the Web backends, moved onto `@migaia/storage-host`, call the host's shared rules and change controller, but no public or author entry exposed them (resolved as `/authoring/backend` plus `core.createChangeController`/`registerChangeController` and Feature `getChangeController`);
- a borrowed backend view (cache and archive `getPublishedBackend`) must answer `has`/`use` for the original store, but the contract's raw/frozen-base admission rejects a wrapper (resolved as read-only `hasStorageCapability`/`useStorageCapability`);
- persist inherits a concurrency budget and memory/IndexedDB/SQLite share one in-process key-lock port, but `runWithConcurrency` required `policy`, the attempt's canonical key identity was not readable, and no install-window lock port existed (resolved as optional `policy`, a read-only identity accessor and a host lock port).

Each consumer step described the call in prose ("复用迁入 host 的共享规则", "借用已发布后端", "与 memory 相同的宿主中立进程内键锁组合") without naming the symbol it imports. So neither side's fence held the edge, and nothing compared them.

**Root cause:** `references/v2-program.md` (second paragraph) requires every public symbol a child's fences or steps reference to have a producer, but that only constrains symbols a step names. A step that describes a cross-leaf call in prose passes, and `references/review.md` L3 dry-runs one leaf against the current code, not against its siblings' declared fences. `references/v2-migration.md` asks for "the real read/call edge" per consumer only when an owner moves, and it is not applied to the consumers inside the same program that the move creates.

## OD-135 bold BC declarations are invisible to preflight requirement detection

Observed 2026-10-23 in migai `docs/repo/error-source-domains.sdd.md`, revision 2–4: the body declares `- **BC1** （破坏性变更）`, while `validate.ts validate` reports `handoff.preflight.required:false` and `reasons:[]`. It still emits the eight change-base RED blockers, but the BC-specific candidate/preserve requirements are skipped. The user's prompt independently required preflight, so this run did not treat the false flag as permission to skip it. Evidence: `docs/repo/scratch/exec/error-source-domains.validate-r2.json` and `error-source-domains.validate-r3.json`. No skill code or SDD markers were changed to work around this result.

**Root cause:** `scripts/validator/domain/v2-preflight.ts:120-123` — `DECLARED_BC` matches only an unformatted list ID immediately after the bullet, unlike this repository's bold clause IDs. A semantically identical Markdown emphasis change silently removes a BC from `declaredChanges()` and its required preflight checks.

## OD-136 disposable dependency links incorrectly share pnpm writable task state

Observed 2026-10-23 in migai error-source-domains preflight P0/P2. pnpm 12.11.2 rejects the disposable node_modules/.pnpm-task-run-state-v1 symlink with "Refusing to use task run state directory ... because it is a symbolic link or not a directory". Both intended baseline gates stop before their actual work. Full logs: docs/repo/error-source-domains.sdd.md.preflight.json.logs/P0.log and P2.log.

**Root cause:** `scripts/validator/domain/v2-replay.ts`, `linkInstalled()` — links every node_modules entry as if it were an immutable installed dependency, including pnpm's writable per-run metadata.

Local minimal correction: omit only `.pnpm-task-run-state-v1` from copied dependency links, allowing pnpm to create private state inside the disposable tree. No command, threshold, package source, hook, or pnpm safety check is changed. Verification will be the affected preflight gates, not a new test framework.

Additional evidence for OD-136, 2026-10-23: after the minimal task-state correction, rerun P2 passed and P0 reached actual storage-web TypeScript errors instead of pnpm's symlink refusal. A9's six real cases all failed on the required source assertions (11 assertion failures, no unrelated case failure), but its preparation also logged an ignored install attempt rejecting `node_modules/.pnpm` as a non-real workspace hoist directory. This is the same linkInstalled ownership assumption; no further store-copy mechanism was added because that attempt did not block the observed wire cases and a broader installer-layout change is outside this design task. Full evidence remains in P0/P2/P23 logs.

settled_observations.evidence: preflight.ts records the full start-of-run commit and passes it through materialise() to exportTree(), so every item in one run exports that exact commit and a concurrent commit cannot change the tree; the host's local correction is kept as the fix.
settled_observations.text:
## OD-137 preflight records one HEAD but exports mutable HEAD for every item

Observed 2026-10-23 during migai error-source-domains preflight: the shared branch advanced from 9f5bad431 through f93de84e/e30ef0a4 to a5b219a0 while independent work continued. Current reports legitimately retain different per-item start records across partial runs, but the tool also captures run.head once and calls materialise/exportTree with literal HEAD for every item. A commit during a long run can therefore change the exported tree without changing the recorded run.head; earlier results cannot establish one coherent latest baseline.

**Root cause:** `scripts/preflight.ts`, main/runItem/materialise — provenance is captured at main entry but the captured immutable revision is never passed to exportTree.

Local minimal correction: record the full start-of-run commit and pass it through materialise into exportTree. Every selected item in one run now uses that exact existing commit. No repository commit, reset, hook, gate, waiver or private checkout protocol is added. The next complete preflight will retain its single snapshot record; historical partial results stay historical rather than being relabelled.

Observed 2026-10-23 in migai error-source-domains review round 6, revision 9. R6 explicitly names Go Host use/unUse, but A9/P25 drove only use; leaving the independent unUse override on wireError's endpoint default would pass. R2 requires every reader to reference its owner's constant, but A6 searched new literals only inside the owner package, missing cross-package inline replacements. No mechanical check expands operation names or reader ownership into their semantic universe. Local design correction: A9 names and separately exercises both Host operations; A6 classifies each new domain across all package src, with a focused witness rejecting new inline literals in the two known cross-package readers. No generic validator, production mechanism or new requirement is introduced.

settled_observations.evidence: v2-document.ts childPath() now bounds a child by the program directory's parent (the document tree) or the resolved repository, so an authoritative program outside --repository with children in sibling directories no longer reports false SDD_V2_PATH_ESCAPE.
settled_observations.text:
## OD-140 external authoritative program docs fail sibling-path checks with an isolated code repository

Observed 2026-10-23 in migai rpc-host program review. The supported invocation used the authoritative program at /Users/kaeo/workspack/migai/docs/rpc-host/rpc-host-program.sdd.md with --repository /tmp/migai-rpc-host-review-20261023 at 4af04a168f09a4c852fbd94e7f8f6c2d3f335a03. validate reported 9 child-path-escape errors and 44 consequent missing module references (53 blockers), although all sibling docs exist beneath the authoritative docs root. Mirroring the same documents into the code worktree removed these errors without changing their relative paths or code. Evidence: docs/rpc-host/scratch/exec/program-review-20261023/validate-before.json, validate-before-mirror.json and import-manifest.json. No validator code or thresholds changed.

**Root cause:** scripts/validator/domain/v2-document.ts:197-215 binds childPath to only the program directory or the explicitly selected code repository; references/v2-contract.md permits an SDD outside --repository but provides no independent authoritative document-tree bound for sibling children. Separate document and code roots therefore produce false path escapes.

settled_observations.evidence: The blockers are truthful: an item set that leaves required coverage out is incomplete. references/authoring/report.md now says that when the user limits preflight to some items, the author runs only those and leaves the remaining requirements as SDD_V2_PREFLIGHT_REQUIRED named pending authorization, never as unauthorised runs or weakened items. No scoped evidence mode is added to v2-preflight.ts.
settled_observations.text:
## OD-142 narrow review preflight activates all-acceptance and all-script implementation gates

Observed 2026-10-23 in rpc-host review. The user explicitly limits preflight to BCs, unproven kernel capabilities and tree shaking, forbids unrelated tests and implementation. Adding those real preflight items makes checkPreflight require RED for every Must-Ship acceptance and every script named test/typecheck across future writes, including conformance, suite-parity and packed gates. These are evidence-policy blockers, not missing design structure. Evidence: validate-rpc-plugin-process-r4.json and validate-rpc-contract-remote-shapes-r4.json.

**Root cause:** scripts/validator/domain/v2-preflight.ts:255-283 derives its complete change/gate universe from all requirements and writes after any item is declared; it has no scoped-review evidence mode. The source/target API also does not yet exist, and manufacturing existence stubs would violate the requested preflight method. Preserve truthful blockers rather than run forbidden suites or mark future behavior verified.

### OD-141 additional evidence: recurrence during the formal implementation preflight (2026-10-24)

Observed 2026-10-24 in the migai rpc-host program second round (11 leaves, 412 items, HEADs 9b8ae91b/8ece4bd3/1fe0abaf). The same shared-shim corruption came back twice while running the formal preflight, not only in review. Mechanism, now identified: pnpm 12 `verifyDepsBeforeRun` runs on every `pnpm run`/`pnpm exec` inside the disposable tree. Because `linkInstalled()` links `node_modules/.bin` back to the source worktree, that automatic dependency check rewrites the source worktree's shims to the disposable tree's absolute path. 99 shims pointed into deleted `sdd-preflight-*` directories at the first scan, and a contract batch failed before loading tests. Two ordinary `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` runs exited 0 but restored nothing, so exit 0 is not evidence of recovery. Only a forced offline relink (`--frozen-lockfile --offline --ignore-scripts --force`, 178 reused, 0 downloaded) brought the stale count to 0. The host then had to set `pnpm_config_verify_deps_before_run=false` in every outer window and rewrite 88 item commands from the `.bin/vitest` shim to `node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs`. Evidence: `docs/rpc-host/scratch/exec/program-impl-20261023/formal-shim-recovery*.json`, `formal-shim-unified-post-install-scan.json`, in the worktree `/private/tmp/migai-rpc-host-program-20261024`.

**What a fix needs:** `linkInstalled()` must not share writable generated state. Either give each disposable tree its own `.bin` (regenerated or copied, never symlinked), or run items with pnpm's dependency verification disabled by the runner itself. The host should not have to discover and patch this per run.

settled_observations.evidence: references/v2-contract.md: a gate that imports a sibling workspace package through its built entry carries that package's git-ignored build output (dist, generated glue, stamps) in inputs, and a resolution error naming a git-ignored path is a missing input, not RED. No ERROR outcome or workspace-graph derivation was added to preflight.ts.
settled_observations.text:
## OD-143 preflight items cannot reach git-ignored build outputs unless the author lists every one as `inputs`

Observed 2026-10-24 in the same run. `materialise()` exports HEAD with `git archive`, so the disposable tree has no `dist/`, no wasm-pack glue and no dist stamps. Gate items for packages whose tests or type checks import a sibling workspace package through its public entry fail before the oracle runs: host P163/P164/P165 (store-worker typecheck:test, unit, e2e types; TS2307 / "Failed to resolve entry") and P170 (tray types). The registry and public-exports items (error-source P6, integration P70) failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for `store-wasm` runtime glue, and the 32-owner aggregate P7 was refused by the store-wasm dist-stamp guard. Each failure looked like a product regression until the host traced it, then hand-listed the exact `packages/<dep>/dist` paths, glue, binary and `.input-digest.json` per item and re-ran. Evidence: `formal-consumer-own-dist-input-correction.json`, `formal-wasm-store-input-precheck.json`, `formal-wasm-input-corrected-validate-*.json`.

**Root cause:** `references/v2-contract.md` documents `inputs` for generated docs and local registries, but neither the reference nor `preflight.ts` tells the author that every cross-package import in a workspace needs its build output carried in, nor offers a way to declare that once per leaf. Nothing distinguishes "the environment lacks a build product" from a genuine RED, so environment failures cost a full diagnose-fix-rerun loop each.

**What a fix needs:** one leaf-level declaration of required build outputs (or derivation from `writes` plus the workspace graph), and an ERROR outcome ("input missing") instead of FAIL when a resolution error names a git-ignored path.

settled_observations.evidence: references/authoring/verify.md: check each new acceptance assertion against the existing clauses it touches (construction atomicity, lifecycle, routing); a contradiction is a design conflict settled before handoff.
settled_observations.text:
## OD-146 new acceptance assertions are never checked for conflicts with existing normative clauses

Observed 2026-10-25/26 in migai `docs/rpc-host/rpc-host-core.sdd.md` (R22 topology evidence). The author added acceptance assertions that contradicted clauses already in the same SDD, and validate, preflight and review all passed. Two examples:
- "a wrong secret on c refuses only the b–c hop, other namespaces keep working" contradicts the existing atomic cold-construction and partial-rollback rule;
- "a forwarding loop between b and c is rejected with `FORWARD_LOOP`" contradicts the directory split-horizon rule, which makes the reflected route unknown, so R20 rejects it locally first.

The unattended host only discovered each conflict after implementing it. It stopped twice (`RESUME-R22-03-COLD-TRANSACTION`, `RESUME-R22-01-SPLIT-HORIZON-LOOP`) and needed user rulings, plus a third stop for the public-install follow-up.

**Root cause:** `references/authoring/verify.md` — the acceptance-quality candidates check coverage, discrimination and scope of each assertion against its own requirement, but no step requires checking a new acceptance assertion against the existing normative clauses it touches (construction atomicity, lifecycle, routing). So a contradiction between a new oracle and an old rule is invisible until the host implements it.

## OD-147 removal inventory misses documentation examples and e2e fixtures in sibling packages

Observed 2026-10-26 in migai rpc-host program.
- **First case:** SC10 removed the `@migaia/rpc-plugin-process/adapters/*` entry points. Four executable `doc-test` examples in `packages/supervision/USEGUIDE*.md` still imported them. `make docs-examples` failed them only in the final gate, and the host stopped (`RESUME-DOCS-SUPERVISION-NATIVE-LAUNCHER-EXPORT`).
- **Second case:** moving browser Workers to rpc-plugin-browser left a thread-package browser e2e fixture (`WebThreadLauncher` with `threadPlugin`) without a disposition. That was another final-gate stop (`RESUME-THREAD-BROWSER-OWNED-ORACLE-DESTINATION`).

settled_observations.evidence: references/dispatch.md Decisions lists what the host decides alone (fixture aligned with documented usage, retiring a test outside the ruled scope with its destination, reshaping an assertion to a ruled data shape, implementation-level additions under an existing owner) and what escalates (semantics, scope, existing public API, budgets or thresholds, conflicting rulings).
settled_observations.text:
## OD-148 handoffs give the unattended host no explicit list of decisions it may take itself

Observed 2026-10-26: the unattended Codex host escalated about a dozen `needs_ruling` items in one day. Several of them existing rules could already decide:
- aligning a fixture with documented public usage;
- retiring a test whose platform is out of the ruled scope, with its destination recorded;
- reshaping an assertion to an already-ruled data shape.

The handoff said "decide what existing clauses decide", but the host, bound by strict no-semantic-relaxation rules, treated each of these as a user decision. Every stop cost a round trip with the user.

**Root cause:** `references/dispatch.md` — the dispatch and close protocol defines only what the host returns and when the parent re-dispatches or asks the user. It never gives the host an explicit list of decisions it may take alone, versus the ones that must escalate (semantics, scope, public API, budgets), so a cautious host escalates everything.

settled_observations.evidence: references/v2-migration.md: a moved or replaced owner also lists the capability combinations the old code accepted (backend kind x capability x feature) with the mechanism that made each work; a combination whose mechanism the move deletes is preserved, narrowed as a BC, or rejected.
settled_observations.text:
## OD-149 migration inventory lists call edges, not the capability combinations the old implementation allowed

Observed 2026-10-23 in migai during implementation. The old storage-web allowed a user-injected async-only raw KV (`get`/`set` only) to back an entity `unique` index, made safe within one process by a global coordinator. The storage-host move (D-MOVE) removes that coordinator. No leaf noticed that this combination then has no atomic compare/write, until the implementing host found it and had to stop for a ruling. Earlier in the same run the host also stopped on three missing cross-leaf entry points (OD-134). Every leaf had passed review and `validate`.

**Root cause:** `references/v2-migration.md` asks for each consumer's read/call edge and compatibility treatment, but not for the capability matrix the old owner supported: each combination of backend kind, capability and feature the old code accepted, with the mechanism that made it work. A move that deletes that mechanism (here, the coordinator) therefore passes, because no combination row ties the deleted mechanism to a behaviour that must be preserved, narrowed with a behaviour change, or rejected.

settled_observations.evidence: references/v2-contract.md: a numeric budget or threshold states its provenance, a user value or an author estimate with its measured baseline; an unmeasured estimate does not block, and a measurement that misses it returns to the author, not to the user as a broken ruling.
settled_observations.text:
## OD-150 an unmeasured author-chosen budget becomes a hard gate that only the user can lift

Observed 2026-10-23 in migai. During the program review the user ruled only that a browser bundle budget be set "relative to main, with unused capabilities tree-shaken". The host picked the number itself: 1.15× minified/gzip, recorded in the root as A-bundle-1 with "仅未来实施测量，本轮没有体积结果", plus 250000 instantiations / 5 s for type cost. During implementation, after 8h 52m, the run measured 1.263× minified and 1.297× gzip on the fixed baseline. All other slice assertions and browser checks passed. The gate blocked every later batch, and the host stopped for a user decision because "weakening a user ruling" is reserved for the user, although the user never gave that number (`docs/storage-contract/scratch/exec/browser-bundle-budget-proposal.md`).

**Root cause:** `references/authoring/report.md:3` and `references/v2-contract.md:51` require preflight only for a leaf that declares a scaling gate. They do not ask a numeric budget to state its provenance (a user value or an author estimate) or its baseline measurement, and do not limit what an unmeasured estimate may block. So a design-time guess, never measured and written into a program root that `validate` does not check (OD-126), carries the authority of a user ruling and a hard batch gate until someone measures it.

settled_observations.evidence: preflight.ts runs every command with pnpm_config_verify_deps_before_run=false, so pnpm's dependency check inside a disposable tree no longer rewrites the repository's .bin shims through the linked node_modules; the host no longer sets it per window or rewrites item commands.
settled_observations.text:
## OD-141 preflight dependency linking lets pnpm rewrite source-worktree executable shims

Observed 2026-10-23 in rpc-host review at 4af04a16. preflight.ts materialises a throwaway tree and v2-replay.ts:175-207 linkInstalled symlinks each package node_modules/.bin directory back to the source worktree. pnpm exec/run in that tree rewrites the shared Vitest shim to the disposable tree absolute path. After cleanup the next source-worktree family coverage command fails MODULE_NOT_FOUND for sdd-preflight-WzfXti/.../vitest.mjs before collecting tests. The first ordinary offline frozen installation did not regenerate shims. Both subsequent coverage attempts stopped before collection; the same operation was not retried again. A forced offline dependency recreation is used only to restore generated state. Evidence: program-review-20261023/coverage-after-environment-failure.log and dependency-shim-restore.log. No production source or runner change.

**Root cause:** `scripts/validator/domain/v2-replay.ts` — writable executable shims remain shared, although .pnpm-task-run-state-v1 is explicitly excluded. The disposable runner therefore mutates generated state outside its captured writes. Record the defect; do not patch the skill during this scoped review.

settled_observations.evidence: references/v2-contract.md: item commands hold no host execution policy (exclusive windows, locks, time caps); the host wraps each preflight.ts run --only <IDs> call. No --wrap hook was added: --only already lets the host batch.
settled_observations.text:
## OD-144 item commands wrapped in the repository's exclusive window deadlock or serialise under an outer runner

Observed 2026-10-24. Design-time items in five leaves (host P91–P95, process P91, contract P91, coroutines P91/P92, error-source P0 and others) embedded `node scripts/exclusive-window.mjs run ... --` in their own commands, because the repository requires heavy commands to run inside that window. A formal run of several items must itself hold the window, so the inner runner waits on the port the outer one holds until its `--wait` expires (exit 75). The host had to strip every inner wrapper and wrap each `preflight.ts run --only <batch>` call once, splitting batches under the 45-minute cap by hand (120 windows in total). Evidence: `second-final-formal-window-history.json`.

**Root cause:** `references/v2-contract.md` — the skill has no notion of a host-level execution wrapper. Authors put repository execution policy into item commands, where it is wrong at run time, and `preflight.ts` has no option to apply a wrapper per item or per batch.

**What a fix needs:** a documented rule that item commands never contain host execution policy, plus an optional per-item wrapper hook (for example a `--wrap` template) in `preflight.ts`, so batching and time caps are not hand work.

settled_observations.evidence: SKILL.md (commands table) and references/v2-contract.md now say each item runs in a private throwaway Git repository the runner creates, whose scaffolding commits are not project commits, so preflight never skips or needs to bypass a project hook.
settled_observations.text:
## OD-145 the private preflight commit's `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` reads as a hook bypass to unattended hosts

Observed 2026-10-23/24. An unattended Codex host refused to run the formal preflight for a whole night. It read `preflight.ts` lines 81–99 (`git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` commit) as conflicting with the user's "never bypass hooks / never `--no-verify`" rule, and reported 93 REQUIRED plus 3 STALE items as "blocked" until the user ruled that the throwaway repository is not a project commit. The source comment says so (OD-84), but `SKILL.md` and the preflight reference do not, and hosts read the rule before they read the code.

**Root cause:** `SKILL.md` — the commands table and the preflight reference never say the disposable tree is a private repository, so its hook-less commits read as a project hook bypass.

**What a fix needs:** one sentence in `SKILL.md` and the preflight reference: the disposable tree is a private repository created by the runner; its scaffolding commits are not project commits, and running preflight never requires or permits skipping hooks in the user's repository.
